rationale: Cold-start, iteration 0 (directions_tried empty). M1 pass/fail currently relies on a subjective 'CSV replay visual check' to distinguish hopping from alternating walk, yet the ENTIRE post-M1 decision-branch tree (raise airtime threshold / raise single_foot_contact scale / raise orientation scale / etc.) requires objectively telling apart 'gait emerged' vs 'still hopping' vs 'cadence too fast'. All known_dead_ends are reward-shaping terms; V13's thesis is minimal-reward emergent gait, so the highest-leverage NEW direction hardens M1's validation instrument rather than touching reward design. Reusable as the standard eval harness for M2 and M3.
description: Build an objective, automated gait-analysis pipeline that classifies the policy locomotion mode (hopping vs alternating walk vs stand) and quantifies gait regularity from per-foot ground-contact and foot-height signals logged during eval rollouts of TASK_20260612_050. Replaces the subjective 'CSV replay visual check' in the M1 success criteria with reproducible metrics derived from logged per-foot contact-force and foot-height trajectories: (a) L-vs-R contact anti-phase lag normalized to stride period, (b) double-support fraction, (c) single-stance fraction, (d) cadence (step frequency). Outputs an 'alternation score' plus a classified locomotion-mode label per rollout, enabling automated M1 pass/fail and unambiguous selection among the M1 decision branches.
hypothesis: Under V13's single_foot_contact reward, an emerged ALTERNATING gait manifests as a stable ANTI-PHASE relationship between left and right foot ground-contact signals (contact-phase lag about 0.5 of stride period, low variance across strides, double-support fraction below 0.2). A HOPPING policy instead shows near-zero phase lag (both feet contact ground simultaneously) and high double-support fraction. Therefore a quantitative alternation score (0 = simultaneous or hopping, 1 = perfect anti-phase) at or above 0.7, together with the already-tracked single_foot_contact reward term above 0.8, objectively confirms that the single physical contact constraint is sufficient to self-emerge alternating gait (the V13 core hypothesis), WITHOUT requiring gait clocks, reference trajectories, or symmetry penalties.

expected_metric.alternation_score: >= 0.70 (normalized cross-correlation lag of L vs R foot-contact signals relative to stride period; 0 = hop, 1 = perfect anti-phase)
expected_metric.single_stance_fraction: >= 0.40 per foot (meaningful swing phase per leg)
expected_metric.coverage: above thresholds hold for >= 80% of steady-state walking-rollout steps
expected_metric.corroborating_existing_metric: single_foot_contact reward term > 0.8 (already tracked in training)
expected_metric.pass_criterion: alternation_score >= 0.70 AND double_support_fraction < 0.20 AND single_foot_contact_reward > 0.8 => M1 gait-emergence objective PASS

distinct_from_dead_ends: Orthogonal to every known_dead_ends entry (CoT efficiency tau-dot-q, walk_decay, efficiency weak or dominant, swing_foot_forward unbounded, sigma 0.08, tracking weight 2.5, efficiency-vs-landing conflict, symmetry, Schumacher V10-V12 route). Adds NO reward term and changes NO reward weights; it is a pure measurement or diagnostic over eval-rollout contact and foot-height logs.
blocks_on: Eval rollouts and contact-force plus foot-height logs from TASK_20260612_050 checkpoints (active external training). If logs are not yet available, direction execution pauses until training produces checkpoints.
next_step: Confirm TASK_20260612_050 status and obtain a trained checkpoint eval-rollout logs (per-foot contact force and foot z-height vs time). Then implement the contact-threshold to binary contact signal to cross-correlation phase-lag to alternation-score pipeline and apply it to M1.
